notes: Workstream E, dates and historical events. 63 real dates in 9 themed sets of 7, in ascending year order inside each set. Fact-check, Nov 2, 2026: every year was looked up in the English Wikipedia article named in sourceUrls (62 found directly in the article text, and the Columbus article was then corrected to Voyages of Christopher Columbus, which gives 1492); day-level details in 'source' (for example 15 June 1215, 14 October 1066) are standard and agree with the named reference works. Two dates are conventional and are worded that way (476 and 1337). The Web date (1991) is worded as 'announced to the public' (6 August 1991 summary by Tim Berners-Lee; CERN placed the technology in the public domain in 1993). Three years appear in two sets (1869, 1914, 1991): if two sets are mixed in one drill, accept both events for that year or keep them apart. Dates already used by the v0.11 Scriptorium timelines (1957 to 1980 space, flight and medicine) are deliberately not repeated. No living person is named. Nothing implies endorsement. Hooks (the event pictures) are suggestions; the player may swap them. Major words are computed from MAJOR_PAIRS in src/data/content.js (the shipped default list); if the player has edited their own list (p.major) the app should show their words instead.

where.drill: Facts drill variant src "dates" (see "drillVariant"), from the Week 20 pairs slot and as optional extra practice from M5.
where.trial: The nine real sets are appended to TIMELINES, so the existing Scriptorium trial can draw them. A new trial "year_hall" (event to year, Major pictures) unlocks at M7.
where.eventHall: Year Round, a scaled-down scored round (see "eventHallRound").
where.yourOwnText: Not used. The player may type their own dates as lines of a text, but these shipped sets are not text.

gates.eventHallYearRound: M10 (the Event Hall opens at the M10 gate)

method.name: Year Pictures on a Timeline
method.summary: Give each date two pictures and one scene. The year is the two Major System pictures side by side (the first two digits, then the last two). The event is a hook picture. Put the scene on the next desk or stop of a timeline route, so the order of events holds the order of the years.
steps: Pad the year to four digits. 1066 is 10 and 66. 476 is 04 and 76. 44 BCE is 00 and 44, and you keep BCE in the label of the set.
Say each pair as its Major picture: 10 is toes and 66 is judge.
Choose a hook for the event: a bright eye over a hasty meal for Hastings.
Make one scene that holds the hook, the two year pictures and the desk: a judge with ten toes pulling an arrow out of a bright eye, standing on the first desk.
Run the desks in order. Because the desks go forward in time, you always know roughly which century you are in, so on a ladder you may learn the last two digits only.

ladder.name: Last two digits
ladder.rule: The player answers only the last two digits (66 for 1066). The century is shown on the set title or by the order of the desks.

ladder.name: Full years
ladder.rule: The player answers the full year (1066). BCE years need the letters BCE or BC.

ladder.name: Put them in order
ladder.rule: The seven events are shown shuffled, with no years. The player puts them in order along the desks. One point for each event in its right place.

method.honest: Pictures are a good way to keep a bare year such as 1066 attached to an event. They do not teach why anything happened. The Major System costs time at first: for a year you already half know, a plain check is quicker. Use pictures for the years you keep mixing up.

workedExamples.scene: A judge with ten toes pulls an arrow out of a bright eye at the first desk of the hall.
A tiny ship rolls on a tire towards a giant dove, carrying a bone as its mast.
A duck wearing a watch fob swings a giant key at a stone fortress.

scoring.accuracyFirst: Each question is right or wrong. A year is right only when every digit is right (no off-by-one credit). Feedback shows the true year and the date detail from "source" in plain words.
scoring.skillEstimate: The facts skill (structure) only, through the normal drill result. Event Hall and trial results never change skill estimates.
scoring.speed: No timer on recall. Time is shown only as a personal best when accuracy is 85 percent or higher.
scoring.trial: year_hall passes with 6 of 7 straight after studying and 5 of 7 after 7 days. A miss costs nothing and fresh dates come on the next try.
scoring.delayed: Drill sets go to p.sets as usual and are probed at 1, 7 and 30 days.

drillVariant.spec: { t: 'facts', n: 7, s: 120, src: 'dates', ask: 'event'|'year'|'order', yearPart: 'last2'|'full', set: '<set id>' (optional) }
drillVariant.items: { cue: '1066' or event label, answer: event label or year, hook, pairs: ['10','66'], accepts: [...] }. For ask 'order' the item is { cue: 'Hastings', answer: '4' } (the position 1 to 7).
drillVariant.recallMode: ask 'event' and 'year' use the cued mode with the existing forgiving matcher plus the alternates in accepts; ask 'order' uses the cued mode and a number answer.
drillVariant.save: No new record. Stored in p.sets with the spec; the probe reads cue and answer. Add the template check in store.js only if new keys (src, ask, yearPart) are validated.

trialYearHall.title: The Hall of Years
trialYearHall.method: Dates and timelines: two Major System pictures for the year, one hook for the event, all on the same desk.
trialYearHall.setup: Beyond the flooded floor, a long hall of tall brass years has lost its labels. The Tide rubbed every date from the shelves, but the events are still carved above them.
trialYearHall.intro: Seven events, seven desks. Make a year picture and an event picture for each, and put them on the desk. An echo will ask you for the year of each event. You will be asked again after a week.
trialYearHall.pass: You say all the years and the brass labels slide back into their frames, one after another. Ennick tilts a small year tablet out of the last frame and hands it to you.
trialYearHall.miss: A few years slid away, which is ordinary for numbers. Look at only those, make the picture stranger, and tomorrow there will be a different set of dates.
trialYearHall.builderNotes: Needs a new prize item id (permanent once shipped) and art from tools/asset-studio/prizes.py; owner decision. material() in src/engine/trials.js needs a branch: when t.ask is "year", the study rows show the year as text and the item prompt is "When did this happen? (it was on <desk>)" with the answer the year, alts from accepts. Add the nine real sets to TIMELINES and also keep the three existing real ones. Because both trials draw from TIMELINES, keep "real" true for these.

eventHallRound.realFormat: Not named in the game. A scaled-down scored round where years come from real events.
eventHallRound.howItWorks: You see 10 to 28 real events, each with its year, for a set study time. Then the same events return in a new order and you give the year of each.
eventHallRound.scoring: One point for each year with every digit right. Two trials with fresh events; the better one counts. Practice only: no Lumen, no skill change, best result recorded on the Event Hall ladder.
eventHallRound.notConfirmed: Whether real memory competitions use exactly this format was not verified. The game does not claim it does.
eventHallRound.honest: Years are practised here as a sport skill. Do not read the score as a measure of how much history you know.
eventHallRound.saved: The p.events record from the main plan (best.dates, history). Add the key "dates" to p.events.best in newProfile, migrate and validate.
eventHallRound.pool: All 63 events below, drawn with a seeded shuffle.

sets.title: Rome, crowns and castles
sets.intro: From a famous murder in Rome to the end of the Middle Ages.

events.text: Julius Caesar is killed in Rome by a group of senators.
events.label: Caesar
events.hook: a laurel wreath sliding off a marble head
events.source: Ides of March, 15 March 44 BCE; Plutarch and Suetonius; any standard history of Rome

events.text: The last emperor in the West, Romulus Augustulus, is removed. This is the usual date for the end of the Western Roman Empire.
events.label: Western Rome falls
events.hook: a stone eagle toppling off a column
events.source: Conventional date; historians note the change was gradual

events.text: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day.
events.label: Charlemagne
events.hook: a giant crown on a Christmas tree

events.text: Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein is published.
events.label: Frankenstein
events.hook: a stitched green giant reading under a lamp

events.text: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is first performed in Vienna.

events.text: The Great Exhibition opens in the Crystal Palace in London.

events.text: Stravinsky's ballet The Rite of Spring has its first performance in Paris, and the crowd is noisy.

events.hook: a tower with an enormous crown and a flag

events.text: Pablo Picasso paints Guernica, a huge picture about a bombed town.

events.hook: a giant grey mural with a crying bull

events.text: The Suez Canal opens, joining the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

events.text: The Panama Canal opens to ships.

events.hook: a hat floating through a narrow stone lock

events.text: The first football World Cup is played, in Uruguay.

events.hook: a golden cup spinning on a football

events.text: Roger Bannister runs the first mile in under four minutes.

events.hook: a stopwatch with a banister rail around it
